results.title: Cipolla's pseudoprime construction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a > 1$ be a natural number and let $p$ be a prime that does not divide $a(a^2 - 1)$. Put $n_1 = (a^p - 1)/(a - 1)$, $n_2 = (a^p + 1)/(a + 1)$ and $n = n_1 n_2$. Then $n$ is a Fermat pseudoprime to base $a$: $n > 1$, $n$ is not prime, and $n$ divides $a^{n-1} - 1$.

results.title: Weakly locally nilpotent polynomial at a point
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $u \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ and $r \in \mathbb{Z}$, and let $A$ be a set of natural numbers. Write $u^{(m)}$ for the $m$-fold iterate of $u$ as a map $\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$. Then $u$ is weakly locally nilpotent at $r$ outside $A$ if for every prime $p \notin A$ there is $m \ge 1$ such that $p$ divides $u^{(m)}(r)$. For $A = \emptyset$ this is called locally nilpotent at $r$.

results.title: Nilpotent polynomial at a point
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $u \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ and $r \in \mathbb{Z}$, and write $u^{(n)}$ for the $n$-fold iterate of $u$ as a map $\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$. Then $u$ is nilpotent at $r$ if $u^{(n)}(r) = 0$ for some $n \ge 1$.

results.title: Infinitely many primes avoid $\gamma \alpha^n - \beta$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ be nonzero integers such that $\beta \ne \gamma \alpha^k$ and $\beta \alpha^k \ne \gamma$ for every natural number $k$, that is, $\beta / \gamma$ is not $\alpha^k$ for any integer $k$. Then there are infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p$ divides none of the integers $\gamma \alpha^n - \beta$ with $n \ge 1$.

results.title: Iterates of $x + 1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $u(x) = x + 1 \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ and write $u^{(m)}$ for its $m$-fold iterate as a map $\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$. For every integer $r$ and every natural number $m$, $u^{(m)}(r) = r + m$.

results.title: $x + 1$ is locally nilpotent at $1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $u(x) = x + 1 \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ and write $u^{(m)}$ for the $m$-fold iterate of $u$ as a map $\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$. Then for every prime $p$ there is $m \ge 1$ such that $p$ divides $u^{(m)}(1)$.

results.title: $x + 1$ is not nilpotent at $1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The polynomial $x + 1 \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ is not nilpotent at $1$.

results.title: Classification of locally nilpotent polynomials at $1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A polynomial $u \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ of positive degree is locally nilpotent at $1$ if and only if it has one of the following forms, for some $p \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$: $(x-1)p(x)$ with $p \ne 0$; $-2x + 4 + p(x)(x-1)(x-2)$; $-2x^2 + 7x - 3 + p(x)(x-1)(x-2)(x-3)$; or $u = x + 1$.

results.title: Linear polynomials weakly locally nilpotent but not nilpotent at $1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of primes, and let $c$ range over the positive integers all of whose prime factors lie in $A$. A polynomial $u \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ of degree $1$ is weakly locally nilpotent at $1$ outside $A$ and not nilpotent at $1$ if and only if $u$ is one of: $x + c$; $x - c$ with $c \ne 1$; $cx + 1$ or $-cx + 1$ with $c \ne 1$; or $-2x - 1$, the last only when $2 \in A$.

results.title: Euler–Seidel matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M$ be a type with an addition and let $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be a sequence in $M$. The Euler–Seidel matrix of $a$ is the array $(a_n^k)_{n, k \ge 0}$, with entry $a_n^k$ in position $(n, k)$, defined by $a_n^0 = a_n$ and $a_n^k = a_n^{k-1} + a_{n+1}^{k-1}$ for $k \ge 1$.

results.title: Closed form of the Euler–Seidel matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid and let $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be a sequence in $M$. For all $n, k \ge 0$, the entry $a_n^k$ of the Euler–Seidel matrix of $a$ equals $\sum_{i=0}^{k} \binom{k}{i} a_{n+i}$.

results.title: Rank of a set in a matroid, as a natural number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a matroid $M$ and a set $X$, this is the rank $r(X)$ of $X$ in $M$, the size of a largest independent set of $M$ contained in $X$, taken as a natural number; it is $0$ when this rank is infinite.

results.title: Coefficients of the characteristic polynomial of a matroid
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M$ be a finite matroid on the ground set $E$ with rank function $r$, and let $\chi_M(\lambda) = \sum_{I \subseteq E} (-1)^{|I|} \lambda^{r(E) - r(I)}$ be its characteristic polynomial. For a natural number $j$, this is the integer coefficient of $\lambda^j$ in $\chi_M$, that is, the sum of $(-1)^{|I|}$ over the subsets $I \subseteq E$ with $r(E) - r(I) = j$.

results.title: Absolute coefficients of the characteristic polynomial of a matroid
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M$ be a finite matroid on the ground set $E$ with rank function $r$ and characteristic polynomial $\chi_M(\lambda) = \sum_{I \subseteq E} (-1)^{|I|} \lambda^{r(E) - r(I)}$. For a natural number $k$, $w_k(M)$ is the absolute value of the coefficient of $\lambda^{r(E) - k}$ in $\chi_M$ when $k \le r(E)$, and $w_k(M) = 0$ when $k > r(E)$.

results.title: Log-concavity of the characteristic polynomial of a matroid, statement
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For every finite matroid $M$ on a ground set $E$ with rank function $r$, let $w_k(M)$ be the absolute value of the coefficient of $\lambda^{r(E) - k}$ in the characteristic polynomial $\chi_M(\lambda) = \sum_{I \subseteq E} (-1)^{|I|} \lambda^{r(E) - r(I)}$ when $k \le r(E)$, and $w_k(M) = 0$ when $k > r(E)$. Then $w_{k-1}(M) \, w_{k+1}(M) \le w_k(M)^2$ for every natural number $k \ge 1$.

results.title: Adiprasito–Huh–Katz theorem (Heron–Rota–Welsh conjecture)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite matroid $M$ on a ground set $E$ with rank function $r$, let $w_k(M)$ be the absolute value of the coefficient of $\lambda^{r(E) - k}$ in the characteristic polynomial $\chi_M(\lambda) = \sum_{I \subseteq E} (-1)^{|I|} \lambda^{r(E) - r(I)}$ when $k \le r(E)$, and $w_k(M) = 0$ when $k > r(E)$. Then $w_{k-1}(M) \, w_{k+1}(M) \le w_k(M)^2$ for every natural number $k \ge 1$.

results.title: Instances of FEEDBACK ARC SET
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: An instance of FEEDBACK ARC SET is a triple $(n, E, K)$ consisting of a natural number $n$ (the number of vertices), a finite list $E$ of ordered pairs of natural numbers (the arcs) and a natural number $K$ (the bound).

results.title: Directed adjacency for FEEDBACK ARC SET
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list $E$ of ordered pairs of natural numbers and natural numbers $u$ and $v$, the directed adjacency test returns true when the pair $(u, v)$ occurs in $E$, that is, when $E$ contains an arc from $u$ to $v$, and false otherwise.

results.title: Well-formed FEEDBACK ARC SET instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance $(n, E, K)$ of FEEDBACK ARC SET is well formed when the list $E$ has no repeated entries and every pair $(u, v)$ in $E$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$ and $u \ne v$; that is, $E$ lists distinct arcs, without loops, of a directed graph on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$.

results.title: Feasible FEEDBACK ARC SET instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance $(n, E, K)$ of FEEDBACK ARC SET is feasible when there is an ordering $v_0, v_1, \dots, v_{n-1}$ of the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$, in which each of them occurs exactly once, such that at most $K$ entries $(u, v)$ of the list $E$, counted with repetition, are backward, meaning that the position of $v$ in the ordering is strictly smaller than the position of $u$. Here $v_j$ has position $j$, and a number…

results.title: FEEDBACK ARC SET as a decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The decision problem FEEDBACK ARC SET accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of instances, to an instance $(n, E, K)$ of FEEDBACK ARC SET that is well formed and feasible. Bitstrings that do not decode to an instance are rejected.

results.title: FEEDBACK ARC SET is NP-complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The decision problem FEEDBACK ARC SET belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP reduces to FEEDBACK ARC SET by a polynomial-time many-one reduction.

results.title: Sites of the periodic square lattice
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a positive integer $L$, the sites of the periodic $L \times L$ square lattice are the pairs $(i, j)$ with $i, j \in \mathbb{Z}/L\mathbb{Z}$.

results.title: Numerical value of a spin
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A spin, recorded as a Boolean, has the real value $1$ if it is true and $-1$ if it is false.

results.title: Right neighbour
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a positive integer $L$, the right neighbour of a site $(i, j)$ of the periodic $L \times L$ square lattice is $(i + 1, j)$, with addition in $\mathbb{Z}/L\mathbb{Z}$.

results.title: Upward neighbour
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a positive integer $L$, the upward neighbour of a site $(i, j)$ of the periodic $L \times L$ square lattice is $(i, j + 1)$, with addition in $\mathbb{Z}/L\mathbb{Z}$.

results.title: Energy of an Ising configuration
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a positive integer $L$, let $\sigma$ be a spin configuration on the periodic $L \times L$ square lattice, assigning to each site $p$ a spin $\sigma_p \in \{1, -1\}$. Its energy in the zero-field ferromagnetic Ising model with unit coupling is

results.title: Ising partition function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a positive integer $L$ and real $\beta$, the partition function of the Ising model on the periodic $L \times L$ square lattice at inverse temperature $\beta$ is $Z_L(\beta) = \sum_\sigma e^{-\beta H_L(\sigma)}$, where $\sigma$ runs over all spin configurations on the lattice and $H_L(\sigma)$ is the Ising energy of $\sigma$.

results.title: Finite-volume Ising free energy density
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a positive integer $L$ and real $\beta$, the free energy density of the Ising model on the periodic $L \times L$ square lattice is $\log Z_L(\beta) / L^2$, where $Z_L(\beta)$ is the partition function at inverse temperature $\beta$.

results.title: Ising free energy density along side lengths $n + 1$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$ and real $\beta$, this is the finite-volume free energy density of the Ising model on the periodic $(n + 1) \times (n + 1)$ square lattice at inverse temperature $\beta$, namely $\log Z_{n+1}(\beta) / (n + 1)^2$, where $Z_{n+1}(\beta)$ is the partition function of that lattice at inverse temperature $\beta$.
